sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Niyaj Ahmad
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.218 of 2024, under Section 376, 506 IPC, P.S.
Jalalpur, District Ambedkar Nagar.

3. In terms of the FIR it was alleged that the victim knew the applicant for the last two years and on the false pretext of marriage, the victim was taken to Haryana and physical relations were also formed.

Subsequently, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she was already married, however, she stated that she used to talk to the applicant for the last two years and the applicant had promised to marry her and was now refusing to marry her.
4. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

sentences.text: 5. Considering the statement that the victim was already married and that the entire case is premised on formation of physical relations on the false pretext of marriage and further considering the fact that the relationship continued over a span of two years, the applicant who is in custody since 29.06.2024 is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Sugreev @ Sugreem be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
